subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs VendorX
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs VendorX

Hi Dana / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + demo and suggested next steps so we stay aligned while you finish internal scoring. I pulled the highlights into the attached scorecard and a short test plan.

Top pain points you emphasized:
- High and unpredictable inference cost for peak query patterns (billing variability impacts ROI).
- Latency SLOs for user-facing features: consistently <200ms p95 required.
- Data isolation + auditability for regulated workflows (SOC2 + audit logs).

Goals we heard:
- Move to a predictable, reserved-capacity model for core inference to reduce unit cost.
- Keep a hosted API for burst and sandboxing during early rollout.
- Provide provable audit trails and per-request logging for compliance.

How Redwood maps to those goals (summary):
- Cost: Dedicated pools + intelligent batching expected to reduce per-token cost by 25-40% based on your forecasted QPS.
- Latency: GPU-optimized runtime with latency SLOs and fallback routing to lower-latency model variants for spikes.
- Compliance: VPC/private deployment plus KMS integration; we can provide sample audit logs and SOC2 artifacts (see attachments).

Decision criteria you mentioned to rank vendors (please confirm):
1) Production p95 latency under 200ms for your 1k token typical payloads.
2) Predictable committed capacity pricing and overage controls.
3) Directability on data retention + audit logs.
4) Vendor support for rollout (canary / A/B) and runbook collaboration.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
- Walnut test: can we run a 2-hour sustained load test at your peak QPS next Thursday (3/4)? (we can coordinate scaling/burst with Dedicated).
- Detailed SOC2 artifact delivery timeline — we'll share our control matrix and sample logs by EOD 3/1.
- Pricing example for a 3-month committed pool + burst capacity — I'll send a draft pricing sheet.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood: share the test plan + scorecard (attached).
2) Acme: confirm Walnut test window and provide a sandbox API key for limited endpoints.
3) Align on a vendor scoring call next Tue (3/2) to review results and any follow-up tests.

Attachments: Acme-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (score breakdown), redwood-test-plan.md (load test details)

Thanks — available for a quick 15-min sync before the test if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Thanks Dana — quick follow-up with the details you asked for and the test plan inline.

Latency sample assumptions (for our internal bench & projected numbers):
- Payload distribution: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (129-512), 5% long (513-1024).
- Model: rwd-13b-q1 (quantized) for baseline + rwd-xxl for high-fidelity cases; we'll surface exact kernel paths used in the run.
- Test harness: we run 10 trials of 30-minute sustained windows and report p50/p95/p99.

Attached: redwood-test-plan.md with step-by-step test harness commands and the Acme-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx with an added integration-effort column.

Test logistics for 3/4 Walnut test:
- Target window: 3/4, 09:00-11:00 PST.
- Redwood action: provision a 4-GPU dedicated pool; enable KV prefix caching; stream results to the shared Drive link.
- Acme action: supply sandbox API key + a small representative subset of real queries (anonymized).

Can Aditya and Markus be on the call? Aditya will own orchestration and Markus will monitor latency traces.

If that looks good I'll schedule a 15-min pre-test sync for 3/3 to run through handoffs.

Best,
Marissa
